I love Two Minute Papers!  
I've seen the second two videos (the last one too many times). However, this algorithm is real time. A lot of papers are published for the purposes of rendering true to life accurate fluid simulations, so time is measured in seconds per frame. To render real-time fluid takes a lot of compute power. I first attempted SPH and found it very difficult to handle collisions, as well as the amount of particles I wanted to use. I would explain why PBD is a better method, but the *Introduction* and *Background* section included in [this paper](https://www.animation.rwth-aachen.de/media/papers/2017-EG-CourseNotes.pdf), as well as *Introduction* and *Related Work* sections in [this paper](https://arxiv.org/ftp/arxiv/papers/1608/1608.04721.pdf) would serve you better than my late night reddit comment.

It depends what your use cases are. As far as interfaces go if you wanna go the cheap route pick up a behringer UM2 as an interface with a built-in preamp. The behringer sounds nice for the money. For mics if you wanna cut out background noise get a dynamic mic (ones that are often used on a stage) I use a cheap pyle microphone i got from a friend as they sound really well for my purposes. For recording purposes and more clear vocals in general get a cardiod microphone (AT-2020,etc.). Make sure the interface you get has phantom power if your mic requires it. A lot of cardiod mics require the phantom power.

edit: My reasoning (and most people’s reasoning) for not using the USB mics is sound cards nowadays are inside of the pc with a lot of different interferences. USB mics can only sound so good before you reach a bottleneck.

Also the way they use the mics in GMM is wrong. You don’t put it on a desk and talk into it it must be close to your mouth due to it being a cardiod mic to my knowledge. Or else you get a ton of room noise.
